question: The mask-blend boundary of the port was generalised from a binary indicator to a solid fraction eps_s (partial_cell_layer, Noble & Torczynski 1998 weight B = eps_s*(tau-1/2)/((1-eps_s)+(tau-1/2)), post-collision reflection). The library code and its unit tests are merged, and the sweep harness exists in run_xval.py, but no verification number has ever been published: does the sub-cell wall actually sit where the analytic solution says it does, and how wrong is the naive upstream float-mask transplant?
unit_of_analysis: one (case, Ny, tau, eps_s, mode) arm; every KPI is a scalar per arm

geometry_convention.cell_centres: integer y, cell k spans [k-0.5, k+0.5]
geometry_convention.partial_row: row 1 of the lattice, solid occupying the low face, so the no-slip interface is at y_b = 0.5 + eps_s
geometry_convention.note: eps_s = 1 is the plain staircase (interface at the shared face y = 1.5) and therefore pins the convention against round 1/2 results

modes.naive_eps: float mask (raw eps_s) fed to the binary bounce layer, i.e. upstream's f*(1-m)+bounce*f*m transplanted verbatim -- pre-collision populations, weight = eps_s
modes.nt_pre: Noble-Torczynski weight B(eps_s, tau) with the pre-collision populations
modes.nt_post: Noble-Torczynski weight B(eps_s, tau) with the post-collision populations (the published NT formulation)

references: closed-form plane Couette u = U*(y-y_b)/H and plane Poiseuille u = g*y*(H-y)/(2*nu) using the *exact* sub-cell y_b, not a snapped wall; the interface offset d_eff is measured by least-squares on the fluid rows only (the partial cell's own macroscopic velocity is a mixture and is excluded)

predeclared_predictions.P1_nt_post_places_the_wall: nt_post: |d_eff - y_b| <= 0.05 dx and profile L2 < 3% for every eps_s in {0.25,0.5,0.75} at tau=0.8 on Couette; Poiseuille to the same bound or better
predeclared_predictions.P2_naive_is_biased: naive_eps: interface offset error >= 0.25 dx at eps_s=0.5, and the error is monotone in (1 - eps_s) across eps_s in {0.25,0.5,0.75}; no closed form is asserted, the measured curve is reported as is
predeclared_predictions.P3_tau_robustness: at eps_s=0.5, |d_eff - y_b| <= 0.05 dx for nt_post at every tau in {0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9} (the NT weight is tau dependent; the wall position must not be)
predeclared_predictions.P4_reflect_choice_matters: nt_pre is worse than nt_post at eps_s in {0.25,0.5,0.75} (the NT model reflects post-collision populations); falsifier: both agree to <= 0.05 dx, in which case the reflect choice is immaterial for a converged static case and the 'post' default is a preference, not a correctness requirement
predeclared_predictions.P5_eps_one_collapse: at eps_s = 1 exactly, naive_eps, nt_pre and nt_post reduce to the staircase bounce result -- profile L2 and peak error agree within 1e-9 relative

falsifiers: any nt_post arm with |d_eff - y_b| > 0.05 dx or L2 >= 15% (owner gate) falsifies the claim that the fractional mask is a verified wall model
a non-monotone naive_eps bias curve falsifies the reading that the raw eps_s weight is a wall-position error of the saturated-cell normalisation
a non-finite population or |u| > 10*U_ref declares the run failed and it is reported, never re-tuned
stopping_rule: step counts are inherited unchanged from round 1/2 predeclared stopping rule (12 viscous e-folding times for Couette + ramp, 3.5*H^2/nu for Poiseuille); no arm is extended after looking at a KPI
analysis_plan: table (case, Ny, tau, eps_s, mode) -> d_eff, offset error in dx, L2 %, peak error %; verdict by P1..P5; figures: d_eff vs eps_s against the exact y_b line, and L2 % vs eps_s per mode; the numbers are injected programmatically into the report, never transcribed
